title: DLMF 1.15 Summability Methods: Methods of summation are regular if they are consistent with conventional summation.
summary: DLMF 1.15 Summability Methods: Methods of summation are regular if they are consistent with conventional summation.
body: NIST DLMF section 1.15 (Summability Methods) says: "Methods of summation are regular if they are consistent with conventional summation. All of the methods described in § 1.15(i) are regular. For example if uniformly for \theta\in[\delta,2\pi-\delta] . (Here and elsewhere in this subsection \delta is a constant such that 0<\delta<\pi .) uniformly for \theta\in[\delta,2\pi-\delta] . A(r,\theta) is a harmonic function in polar coordinates ( 1.9.27 ), and If f(\theta) is periodic and integrable on [0,2\pi] , then as n\to\infty the Abel means A(r,\theta) and the (C,1) means \sigma_{n}(\theta) converge to at every point \theta where both limits exist. If f(\theta) is also continuous, then the convergence is uniform for all \theta . is the Fourier series of f(\theta) , then the series can be extended to the interior of the unit circle as an analytic function Here u(x,y)=A(r,\theta) is the Abel (or Poisson ) sum of f(\theta) , and v(x,y) has the series representation" Equation 1.15.1 on the page has alt text "s_{n}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_{k}.". Equation 1.15.2 on the page has alt text "\sum^{\infty}_{n=0}a_{n}=s\;\;\;\textit{(A)},". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
